name: Bowling Ball (Ten-Pin)
summary: Glossy unbranded two-colour resin bowling ball with three drilled bores, a 6.5 mm finger bridge and 108 mm conventional surface spans.
description: Glossy unbranded two-colour resin bowling ball with three drilled bores, a 6.5 mm finger bridge and 108 mm conventional surface spans.
author: Yap Wei Jun project / agent-assisted procedural modeling
creation_method: Editable UV sphere with three live manifold Boolean cylindrical cutters. Finger bores are 20 mm diameter and 55 mm deep, with a 6.5 mm edge-to-edge surface bridge (about 26.46 mm centre chord); the thumb bore is 26 mm diameter and 65 mm deep. Both thumb-to-finger spans are 108 mm, measured edge to edge along the shortest spherical surface arc. Radial cylindrical lip angles are asin(bore radius / ball radius); the common grip rotation places the fingers above the thumb on the front hemisphere so the hero and front previews show all three openings. These grip values implement the FIX-1 review specification; they are an illustrative adult conventional grip, not a fit to a particular hand. Generic navy and plum sinusoidal marbling is analytically baked from spherical coordinates to a 1024×512 base-colour PNG and embedded as JPEG. Resin roughness 0.10 with a 0.35 clear coat.

display.origin: Floor contact point under the ball centre.

accuracy_notes: Finger bores are 20 mm diameter and 55 mm deep, with a 6.5 mm edge-to-edge surface bridge. The 26 mm thumb bore is 65 mm deep; both conventional spans are 108 mm edge-to-edge surface arcs. Grip dimensions implement the FIX-1 review specification and are illustrative, not fitted to a hand. Cylindrical flat-bottom radial bores omit lip bevels, inserts, individual pitch and internal core structure. The analytic swirl approximates poured reactive resin. No mass, balance, oil interaction or performance is simulated.

attribution.credit: Original procedural geometry, materials and analytical texture bakes; no external models, fonts, images or logos.
